title: Ultrasmooth Filter (USF)
summary: A two-pole recursive filter fed through a momentum term, giving a very smooth price line that turns with little lag.
descriptionHtml:
The Ultrasmooth Filter is a two-pole recursive filter that reads this bar's price, its two previous prices and its own two previous values. With arg = sqrt(2) * pi / length, it sets c2 = 2 * exp(-arg) * cos(arg), c3 = -exp(-2 * arg) and c1 = (1 + c2 - c3) / 4, then computes USF = (1 - c1) * price + (2 * c1 - c2) * price[1] - (c1 + c3) * price[2] + c2 * USF[1] + c3 * USF[2].

The extra terms on the earlier prices act as a momentum correction: they let the line keep up with a steady trend while the two-pole feedback removes short-term noise. Before the filter has two values of its own it uses the price in their place, so it answers from the first bar.

The length sets how slow a swing must be to pass through. Shorter swings are flattened; slower ones are followed closely.
howToReadHtml:
Read the USF as a smooth trend line that hugs price more tightly than a moving average of the same length. Its slope is the clearest signal: a line turning up marks the slower part of the market turning up, and a line turning down marks the reverse. Crossings of price, or of a second USF with a different length, can time those turns.

The momentum term means the line can overshoot after a sharp reversal. It still describes what price has done, and it lags a true turning point by at least a few bars.

settings.label: Length
settings.html: The cutoff period in bars. Larger values give a smoother line that turns later.

settings.label: Source
settings.html: The price series the filter smooths, the close by default.

faq.q: How does it differ from the Supersmooth Filter?
faq.html: Both share the same two-pole feedback. The Ultrasmooth Filter also feeds in the two previous prices through a momentum term, which tracks a steady trend more closely.
The feedback and momentum terms carry the recent direction forward for a bar or two, so a sudden reversal leaves the line briefly beyond price.
No. Each value uses only this bar and earlier bars, so a value never changes once its bar has closed.

related.title: Ehlers Voss Predictive Filter (VOSS)
related.summary: A two-pole bandpass around one cycle length, with a feedback predictor line that runs a few bars ahead of it so cycle turns show earlier.

related.title: Ehlers 3-Pole Super Smoother Filter (SSF3)
related.summary: A three-pole recursive smoother on price that removes short swings with little lag and almost no overshoot, answering from the first bar.

related.title: Wavelet Denoising Filter (WAVELET)
related.summary: Splits price into a smooth trend and layers of detail, shrinks the small details as noise, and adds the rest back to give a denoised price line.
